messages:
anna: noticed a p99 spike in hosted API around 14:22 UTC, looks like queue depth jumped on a few pods
ops-bot: alert: hosted-api-p99 > 800ms for 3m on prod region-us-west-2
mike: looking at request_queue_length across the pool - a couple of nodes hit 120+ queued requests, normal is < 20
deepa: can you paste the pod ids?
mike: pod/runtime-74f8 and runtime-9c3a showing sustained queues, sending logs
charlie: I pulled the last 10m of kernel selection logs, see this pattern: fallback kernel chosen for large-ctx requests repeatedly:
```
[2026-03-18T14:20:45Z] model=my-model v=1.2.1 ctx=4096 kernels:selected=fallback_matmul reason=kernel_timeout
[2026-03-18T14:20:47Z] model=my-model v=1.2.1 ctx=4096 kernels:selected=fast_attn_v2 reason=success
[2026-03-18T14:20:49Z] model=my-model v=1.2.1 ctx=4096 kernels:selected=fallback_matmul reason=mem_pressure
```
charlie: alternating choices suggests instability in kernel scoring or transient mem bandwidth pressure
jess: I also see KV cache eviction spikes at the same time (evictions/sec went from ~5 to ~300) - that will increase compute per-request
anna: (typo: anna) if KV gets cold we regen keys per token -> extra latency
mike: ran perf sampling on runtime-74f8, CPU flamegraph shows increased time in kernel selector + batcher wake path, not pure model compute
deepa: batching histogram changed — % of small batches (<4 tokens) jumped to 72% during the spike; likely increased per-token overhead
charlie: interesting, our recent batching heuristic change reduced max_wait_ms from 12ms to 6ms in hopes of lower p95, might be over-shrinking batches under bursty traffic
charlie: also kernel selector recently gained a latency-weighted scoring tweak (PR #2123), could be biasing toward fallback under noisy metrics
jess: noisy neighbor theory: one host had a co-located non-runtime job that ramped memory bandwidth, NIC interrupts high in dmesg for that timeframe
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout runtime/1.2.1 completed at 14:10 UTC to 40% canary
mike: timeline: canary rollout started 14:10, alert at 14:22. correlation looks strong
deepa: quick repro: curl the endpoint with mixed ctx sizes, observe queue growth locally when kernel fallback triggers
charlie: profiling artifacts: uploaded pprof cpu and heap at s3://redwood-perf/177210/ - flamegraphs show increased stack time in kernel_selector::score()
jess: mitigation plan candidates:
- revert kernel scoring tweak (PR #2123)
- increase batcher max_wait_ms to 12ms temporarily to form larger batches
- pin model to previous runtime build for canary replicas
mike: short live action: patch batcher config on prod pool to max_wait_ms=12 and bump kv cache reserve to avoid aggressive evictions
anna: opening incident ticket and actions in PagerDuty, assigning oncall eng-runtime team
charlie: I'm starting rollback of PR #2123 in canary now, will monitor p99
ops-bot: rollback job runtime/1.2.1-rollback started at 14:31 UTC
charlie: after changing batcher max_wait_ms on two affected nodes p99 decreased from ~950ms to ~220ms within 3m, queue depth dropped to <30
mike: KV evictions also dropped back to baseline, suggests we avoided cold-cache churn
deepa: will run longer soak for 30m then decide full rollout or pin revert until root cause triaged
jess: follow-ups: create perf test that simulates bursty mixed-ctx traffic, add regression check for kernel selection flapping, add metric for "batch_size_distribution" alerting
anna: created incident-4528, linked PRs: #2134 (batch config), #2135 (rollback), perf test ticket #2136
charlie: next steps: deep root cause — is it scoring heuristic oscillating due to noisy host metrics or memory bandwidth interference? schedule cross-team postmortem with infra and runtime optimizers
mike: thanks folks, marking as in-progress and will update channel with telemetry after 30m soak
anna: :thumbsup:
